page: Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance allocates 2 vCPUs supported by 1 physical core with 2 threads running at a base clock of 3.525 GHz. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory provisioning is set at 32.0 GB, resulting in an allocation of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Storage is configured with 69 GB of local SSD capacity, while graphic compute accelerators are omitted with a GPU count of zero. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor supports standard instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, but does not provide AVX-512 extensions or matrix acceleration instructions such as AMX.

Performance benchmarks reflect strong single-core compute capabilities, achieving a score of 2690.99 in stress-ng single-core tests. Conversely, the low core count impacts multi-core benchmarks, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 2697.38 and Geekbench multi-core scoring 1975.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 32.63 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 22.38 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput is recorded at 2.01 million operations per second, constrained primarily by the two-vCPU ceiling rather than RAM capacity.

From an efficiency standpoint, the hardware profile offers high memory density per compute unit. The instance serves workloads that require substantial working memory but modest processor concurrency, such as dedicated in-memory key-value caching, lightweight database deployments, staging environments, and single-threaded data transformation tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. Running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 32 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 16 GB per vCPU, alongside 69 GB of local SSD storage and no discrete GPU resources. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core CPU performance, balanced by moderate multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth due to the two-vCPU hardware envelope. Cryptographic tasks benefit from hardware-level AES and SHA-NI support, though AVX-512 extensions are absent. The configuration delivers resource efficiency for workloads with large memory requirements and limited parallel compute demands, making it appropriate for modest in-memory caches, small relational databases, memory-resident microservices, and lightweight background data processing.
